CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: when narration safety rejects a reply, RuntimeEngine.turn retries once and calls provider.note_rejection(error.code); CloudflareTurnProvider.note_rejection stores a GENERIC sentence by code (cloudflare.py _REJECTION_FEEDBACK / _GENERIC_REJECTION) and never names the protected term, because naming a protected term would leak it to the narrator. MEASURED PROBLEM: when the player's own command contains the protected phrase (e.g. 'Look for a maintenance access route into the facility.' rejected for 'maintenance access route'), the generic note gives the narrator no way to know what to avoid, so the second reply repeated the phrase in 4 of 4 live turns.

REQUIRED CHANGE (Brandon decided): the retry note may name the rejected term ONLY WHEN THE PLAYER TYPED IT. Rules: (1) Give narration_known_term_leak rejections a structured field on ProposalValidationError (e.g. `term: str | None`, set where narration_safety.py:~205 and ~239 raise) so nobody parses the message text. Other codes leave it None. (2) In the engine's retry branch, compute `typed_term = error.term if error.term and error.term.casefold() in command_text.casefold() else None` (use the command text the player actually typed, not narrator output; use a word-boundary-safe check if a plain substring would let 'card' match inside 'cardigan' or a short term match inside another word) and pass it as an optional argument to the provider's rejection method through the explicit Protocol (default None; providers that ignore it keep working; no isinstance/getattr). (3) CloudflareTurnProvider.note_rejection(code, term=None): with a term, add ONE extra sentence naming it in the same plain style as the existing notes, 12th-grade words, one idea per sentence, following docs/narrator-writing-guide.md, for example: 'The player wrote "<term>". Do not use that exact phrase in your reply. Describe what happens in other words.' Without a typed term the note stays exactly the current generic text (no term, ever). The note still reaches only the next prompt and is then cleared. Keep the single guard retry and the budgets unchanged.

TESTS (extend tests/test_recovery_budget.py; hermetic): (a) player typed the protected phrase -> retry prompt contains the phrase exactly once in the note, in the right sentence; (b) protected term NOT in the player's command -> retry prompt does not contain the term anywhere (the existing sanitized test must still pass); (c) case differences in the typed command still count as typed; (d) a term that appears only inside a longer word in the command does not count; (e) the note is cleared after the retry prompt; (f) a provider without the optional argument still works. Use the words sanitiz, budget, guard and typed in test names. Run full tests/ and ruff check/format on changed files.
